title: Witnesses from outside
note: Remarks about Christ, the Church or Christian ethics from people who did not share the faith. Where an attribution is disputed it says so, because a quotation that will not survive checking is no encouragement at all.

quotes.author: Pliny the Younger
quotes.quote: They were in the habit of meeting on a certain fixed day before it was light, when they sang an anthem to Christ as God, and bound themselves by a solemn oath not to commit any wicked deed, but to abstain from all fraud, theft and adultery, never to break their word, and never to deny a trust when called upon to honour it.
quotes.note: A hostile magistrate, torturing deaconesses for information, could find nothing worse to report than that they kept their promises.

quotes.author: Tacitus
quotes.stance: Roman historian, contemptuous of the sect
quotes.quote: Christus, from whom the name had its origin, suffered the extreme penalty during the reign of Tiberius at the hands of one of our procurators, Pontius Pilatus.
quotes.note: The empire's own record of the crucifixion, written by a man who calls the faith a pernicious superstition.

quotes.author: Julian the Apostate
quotes.quote: These impious Galileans support not only their own poor, but ours as well; everyone can see that our people lack aid from us.
quotes.note: His plan to defeat the Church was to order the pagan priesthood to start copying it.

quotes.author: Lucian of Samosata
quotes.quote: Their first lawgiver persuaded them that they are all brothers of one another, after they have transgressed once for all by denying the Greek gods and by worshipping that crucified sophist himself and living under his laws.
quotes.note: Written to ridicule them, and it still reads as an accurate description of a church.

quotes.author: Flavius Josephus
quotes.quote: He convened the judges of the Sanhedrin and brought before them the brother of Jesus, who was called Christ, whose name was James, and some others.
quotes.note: An outside witness to the family of Jesus, incidental and unforced.

quotes.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
quotes.stance: Enlightenment philosopher, no friend of the Church
quotes.quote: If the life and death of Socrates are those of a philosopher, the life and death of Jesus are those of a God.
quotes.note: He had just finished arguing that revealed religion was unnecessary.

quotes.author: Benjamin Franklin
quotes.quote: As to Jesus of Nazareth, I think the system of morals and his religion, as he left them to us, the best the world ever saw or is likely to see.
quotes.note: Written six weeks before he died, by a man who doubted the divinity in the same paragraph.

quotes.author: Thomas Jefferson
quotes.stance: Deist who cut up his own Bible
quotes.quote: Of all the systems of morality, ancient or modern, which have come under my observation, none appear to me so pure as that of Jesus.
quotes.note: He removed every miracle from the Gospels and still could not get around the ethics.

quotes.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.stance: The fiercest critic Christianity has had
quotes.quote: In truth, there was only one Christian, and he died on the cross.
quotes.note: Meant as an indictment of the Church. It is also a fair description of the standard.

quotes.author: H. G. Wells
quotes.quote: He is easily the most dominant figure in all history.
quotes.note: From a man who spent that same book explaining religion away.

quotes.author: Albert Einstein
quotes.stance: Not a believer in a personal God
quotes.source: Interview with George Sylvester Viereck, The Saturday Evening Post (1929)
quotes.quote: I am a Jew, but I am enthralled by the luminous figure of the Nazarene. No one can read the Gospels without feeling the actual presence of Jesus. His personality pulsates in every word.
quotes.note: Asked whether he accepted the historical Jesus, he answered: unquestionably.

quotes.author: Sigmund Freud
quotes.quote: The commandment 'Love thy neighbour as thyself' is the strongest defence against human aggressiveness.
quotes.note: He raised it only to complain that it is impossible, which is rather the point.

quotes.author: Albert Camus
quotes.source: Address at the Dominican Monastery of Latour-Maubourg (1948)
quotes.quote: What the world expects of Christians is that Christians should speak out, loud and clear, and that they should voice their condemnation in such a way that never a doubt, never the slightest doubt, could rise in the heart of the simplest man.
quotes.note: He told them plainly that their silence during the war had been the scandal, not their creed.

quotes.author: Will Durant
quotes.quote: Caesar and Christ had met in the arena, and Christ had won.
quotes.note: The verdict of a man who wrote eleven volumes of history without needing the faith to be true.

quotes.author: Jürgen Habermas
quotes.stance: Secular philosopher of the Frankfurt School
quotes.quote: Egalitarian universalism, from which sprang the ideas of freedom and a social solidarity, is the direct legacy of the Judaic ethic of justice and the Christian ethic of love. To this day, there is no alternative to it.
quotes.note: One of Europe's leading secular thinkers, conceding the foundation.

quotes.author: Penn Jillette
quotes.quote: How much do you have to hate somebody to believe everlasting life is possible and not tell them that?
quotes.note: He was describing, warmly, a man who had just given him a Bible.

quotes.author: Richard Dawkins
quotes.quote: I do think of myself as a cultural Christian. I would not be happy if we lost all our cathedrals.
quotes.note: Having spent decades arguing the faith was false, he found he did not want the building emptied.

quotes.author: Tom Holland
quotes.stance: Historian who began as a non-believer
quotes.source: Dominion: The Making of the Western Mind (2019)
quotes.quote: The more I saw of the ancient world, the less like us it seemed. My morals and ethics are not Greek or Roman at all. They are thoroughly and ineradicably Christian.
quotes.note: He set out to write about antiquity and discovered he was not an ancient Roman.

quotes.author: Bart Ehrman
quotes.quote: He certainly existed, as virtually every competent scholar of antiquity, Christian or non-Christian, agrees.
quotes.note: Written by a man who left the faith and then spent a book defending its founder's existence.

quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.quote: Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.
quotes.note: The best pagan advice ever written, and completely useless as an excuse.

quotes.author: Seneca
quotes.quote: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
quotes.note: Paul, writing in the same decade, had rather more reality to work with.

quotes.author: Voltaire
quotes.quote: I want my lawyer, my tailor, my servants, even my wife to believe in God, because I think I shall then be robbed and cuckolded less often.
quotes.note: He wanted everyone around him to keep the faith he spent his life attacking.

quotes.author: John Stuart Mill
quotes.quote: Nor even now would it be easy, even for an unbeliever, to find a better translation of the rule of virtue from the abstract into the concrete, than to endeavour so to live that Christ would approve our life.
quotes.note: Written by a man whose father made sure he was never taught to pray.

quotes.author: Napoleon Bonaparte
quotes.stance: Attributed; reported by Count de Montholon
quotes.source: Reported conversation at Saint Helena (attribution disputed)
quotes.quote: Alexander, Caesar, Charlemagne and I myself have founded empires; but upon what did we rest the creations of our genius? Upon force. Jesus Christ alone founded His empire upon love, and at this hour millions of men would die for Him.
quotes.note: The attribution is not secure, which is worth knowing when it is quoted at you.
